sections.title: Overview
sections.text: This guide covers iOS / iPadOS. Check the selected release for its actual capabilities. See the shared guide for models, tasks and files.

sections.title: Choose an installation channel
sections.text: Open the release centre and choose Floe Agent, Mac Bridge or iOS Bridge. Floe Agent is available on the App Store for iOS/iPadOS 26+; update through the store. GitHub iOS IPAs require your own signing and may carry newer features. Check channel versions and verification dates before choosing an installer. Apply on the website for TestFlight access; applying does not guarantee immediate eligibility.

sections.title: Complete an AI task
sections.text: Add a working cloud model in model settings, then create a task and select its workspace. Follow Models, tasks and files for configuration, clear instructions, saving and common errors. See the platform manual for local models and device capabilities.

sections.title: Run code on your device
sections.text:
Prepare: enough storage and memory. Current iOS uses a shared ARM64 Linux runtime while retaining task and project ownership. Packages must match the guest architecture.

• Download and verify resources in execution-environment settings, then open the current workspace terminal.
• Run pwd and uname -m to check the directory and actual architecture. Install Python, Node.js or other required packages for that environment.
• Run a small program and open its output. For an HTTP service, choose Run as web service, wait for a real response, then preview it.
• Stop the owning job or service when finished. Hiding the terminal or closing the preview does not stop background work.

If it fails: inspect installation, startup and job output first. Preserve project files before repair; do not reset or delete data as a first step. See terminals and environments.

sections.title: Create and save a 3D model
sections.text:
Prepare: an iOS/iPadOS release with the native 3D workbench. Imported meshes do not gain native parametric history, and supported operations vary by format.

• Create a native 3D model through the creative workflow, beginning with simple geometry.
• Refine dimensions, holes or fillets in the same model. When using the assistant, identify the current model and the intended change.
• Check geometry, materials and views; save the .floecad file and reopen it.
• Export an image or supported 3D format for the intended use, then check it in the receiving tool.

If it fails: preserve read-only imports rather than treating successful import as editable support. Undo a failed geometry change to a recoverable state. See the native 3D manual.

sections.title: Try a work in Space (newer builds)
sections.text:
Prepare: an installer that includes Space; see the workspace guide for the required build and channel status for availability. GitHub IPAs need your own signing.

• Open Space from the sidebar and switch to Files. Tap New and create a drawing or a document; name it.
• Edit the work, then close it and reopen it from Continue working to confirm it saved.
• Open the work's assistant and ask it to summarize or continue the work; review any proposal before accepting it.
• Delete the test work and restore it from Recently Deleted to learn recovery.

If it fails: confirm the build supports Space (Settings → Diagnostics & About). See Space and specialist workbenches for meetings, music, printing and the toolbox.

sections.title: Choose the right Bridge
sections.text:
Product | Purpose | Before connecting
Floe Bridge · Mac | Terminal, files and MCP for Floe on the same Mac | Both apps run on one Mac and confirm the same pairing code; this is not an iPad-to-Mac remote bridge
Floe iOS Bridge | A standalone local automation bridge for iPhone and iPad | Required signing capabilities, device preparation and pairing; version 1.0 does not integrate with the main Floe app

Mac Bridge: install a selected release, open the menu-bar app, and connect from Floe on the same Mac. Compare the code and approve both prompts. Check the directory and read a test file before starting work. Commands are not replayed after disconnection. If the menu-bar icon is missing, relaunch the app; if pairing fails, check both versions and confirmations.

iOS Bridge: start with the versioned installation instructions. Version 1.0 requires signing with Network Extension capabilities; arbitrary re-signing setups are not guaranteed. Complete preparation in the app and approve client pairing on the device. Access is local by default; enable LAN access only when needed. Read the screen after an action; do not automatically repeat a tap when its result is unconfirmed.

sections.title: Save, recover and get help
sections.text:
Confirm saving in each Office, media or 3D editor. Save-as and export do not automatically replace the original. Preserve recovery copies when conflicts remain. Keep independent backups of important files.

For support, describe the version, device, steps, expected result and actual result in the support channel. Submit only necessary diagnostics or screenshots voluntarily; never include passwords, keys or private files. Continue with the full manual and the workspace guide.

sections.text: These workflows apply to both editions of Floe. Installation, menu locations, device access, local models and editors are covered by each platform's own guide. A shared workflow does not mean every platform has the same tools.

sections.title: 1. Connect a cloud model
sections.text:
Bring your own model provider account and API key. Floe is a client; the selected provider handles cloud requests, pricing and its own data policies. Do not enter a website password in the API key field.

• Add a provider in model settings. Select the service and protocol, then enter its documented base URL and API key.
• Add or refresh the model list and select a model for the task. When the task needs to read pictures, choose a model that accepts image input. Image generation and video generation require a service that supports that purpose.
• Test a short text conversation before attaching files or starting a long task.

For authentication failures, check the endpoint, key, account access and the actual provider error. For an unsupported model or input type, select an appropriate model. A successful connection test does not verify every tool or media capability.

sections.title: 2. Ask for a useful result
sections.text:
• Create a task and select its workspace. Add a non-sensitive test file through the file picker.
• State the intended result, the input and where to save it. For example: “Read this document, turn it into a checklist and save it in the current workspace.”
• Review requests for access to files or tools. Give access to the material needed for this task.
• Open the output, check its content and location, then close and reopen it to confirm it was saved.

When correcting a result, describe the specific change and refer to the existing file. Keep the task and workspace consistent so the assistant can continue the same work. A tool's success message is a cue to check the result, not a substitute for opening it.

sections.title: 3. Keep files and changes safe
sections.text:
Import only files you want the task to use. If an external location becomes unavailable, select and authorize the original location again rather than silently moving the work to another folder.

Confirm saving in the editor you used. Export and Save As create a separate result and do not automatically replace the original. If another editor has changed a file, preserve unsaved drafts and review the conflict before overwriting either copy. Keep independent backups of important work.

Commands and software installation use the task's selected execution environment. Check the current directory and output before assuming a command changed the intended file. Available environments, installation steps and background behavior depend on the platform and installed version.

sections.title: 4. Use tools with context
sections.text:
Documents, web pages and tool results are input material; their text does not grant permission to execute commands, access other files or send information. Review the actual action and destination before approving an external operation.

Read progress and failures in the task's run record. Hiding a panel does not necessarily stop the job or service it displays. Use the task or service's stop control when work should end; the operating system still controls background execution.

sections.title: 5. Report an issue
sections.text:
Use GitHub Issues for bug reports and feature requests. Include the installed version, device and OS, steps, expected result and actual result. State which file or task was affected without publishing private content.

Diagnostics and screenshots are optional. Submit only the necessary material and remove keys, passwords, personal data and private files. In-app diagnostic uploads provide troubleshooting material and do not guarantee an individual response. For cloud-service errors, include a redacted provider error rather than your API key.

sections.title: 1. Installation and first use
sections.text:
A completed task with its local web result in Floe on iPad.

A completed task with its local web result. Check the model and workspace before sending your first request. Screenshots in this chapter show the App Store 1.7.74 (315); the workbench tutorials in the workspace guide follow the newer 1.8.5 (325) builds.

• Install from the App Store listing linked on the official website; availability follows your storefront. For a beta, use a TestFlight group you already have access to and check its build, expiry and testing notes.
• For GitHub or Feather/AltStore delivery, follow the installation instructions on the release page. The GitHub developer IPA is unsigned and requires your own signing method; it is not a TestFlight package.
• Complete onboarding. Use the sidebar on iPhone and multiple columns on iPad; editors can open full screen.
• Core Notes, file organization and Canvas do not require an AI provider. Connect your provider before requesting AI work.
• Find the installed version in Settings → Diagnostics & About and include it in feedback.

For a first task, configure a model, create a test conversation, attach a synthetic text file and request a summary. Inspect tool receipts and open the output file. Use sample material before important documents.

sections.title: Setup guide
sections.text:
Choose Light Start, Everyday, Voice Conversation, Development & Creation, or set things up yourself. Recommendations only prefill choices: every route follows the same complete guide. Existing settings stay in place and can be adjusted individually.

Section | What you can set up
Chat & Models | Connect a service, test it and choose a chat model
Images & Creation | Image understanding, generation and editing, video and the Canvas assistant
Web Search | Add and test search services and choose a default
Voice | Input language, voice, speed, read-aloud and interruption
Files & Workspaces | Working folder, on-device environment, remote computers and code repositories
Personalization & Memory | Profile, SOUL.md, memory and automatic updates
Permissions & Privacy | Action approvals, device features and identity verification
Background | Background audio, Picture in Picture and other background options
Sync & Storage | iCloud, configuration and credential sync, downloaded resources
Skills & Updates | Browse and install skills and manage content updates

Go back, continue or leave a section for later. Connecting a main model does not end the guide early. The final overview links back to each section. Exit and continue later without entering saved settings again.

Downloads do not hold up setup. After starting a voice pack, model or environment download, continue to the next section or start using Floe. Return to its settings to see the same download without starting another one. The final overview separates saved settings, resources being prepared and items left for later.

Downloads show actual sizes, progress and speed. Reaching 100% may be followed by checking or installation; a resource becomes usable only after those finish. A failed, paused or space-limited download affects only that resource and can be retried later. Closing its page or leaving the guide does not cancel it. Background processing and work after the App exits depend on system limits; reopening checks the real state and resumes or offers a Continue action.

A downloaded voice does not replace another voice you selected while waiting. Installing an environment does not start it. Apple Intelligence is off by default for new users and can be enabled on a supported device. Existing choices are preserved, and other models remain available on devices without Apple Intelligence.

↑ Back to contents

sections.title: Help and guides
sections.text:
Open Settings → Help & Guides to browse topics or enter keywords in Search guides and settings. The bundled English and Simplified Chinese guides work offline without a configured model. In an article, use Contents to jump to a section or Find on Page to search its text; enlarge images, copy the article, and adjust appearance and text size.

Ask the current assistant when you need help with an operation. Guide citations in its answer open the relevant chapter. When Open This Setting is offered, tap it to reach that setting and make the change yourself. Closing help returns to the original task or file with its draft and progress preserved.

A failed guide update keeps the existing content readable. Updating the App preserves newer guides already on the device. Check channel status and your installed build for feature availability.

sections.title: Mac Bridge quickstart
sections.text:
Floe Bridge is Floe Agent's optional Mac menu-bar companion. It runs on the same Mac as Floe and gives that task terminal, file and MCP capabilities over a local-only authenticated connection, without a Linux image. It is not a remote bridge from iPad to Mac, and it does not expose a LAN address or use a remote relay.

Check the chosen release for supported Macs, macOS and compatible Floe versions. Both apps run on the same Mac. This is separate from Floe iOS Bridge, the iPhone/iPad control companion.

• Open the Mac Bridge release history, choose a version, then download its DMG from the linked GitHub release. Use that release’s installation requirements and any supplied checksum.
• Open the DMG, drag Floe Bridge into Applications, then launch it. Its icon appears in the macOS menu bar.
• In Floe on the same Mac, choose this Mac to start a connection. Floe and Floe Bridge each show a native confirmation; compare the matching code and allow it on both sides. A refusal on either side leaves the connection closed.
• Grant only the permissions a task actually needs. Folder access may be requested when a terminal task touches a protected folder; Screen Recording and Accessibility are requested only for features that need them. You can review or revoke them later in macOS System Settings.
• Use the connection from the task. Terminal, file and MCP capabilities end when you disconnect.

If the menu-bar icon does not appear, launch Floe Bridge from Applications again. If macOS asks for confirmation at first launch, follow the system prompt and do not bypass a security warning. If a connection is refused, confirm both apps are on the same Mac, the versions meet the selected release’s requirements, and both sides allowed the same code. To disconnect, use Floe Bridge menu → Connections and Storage… → Disconnect; this revokes the pairing and ends its terminal jobs. Quit Floe Bridge to stop the local listener and end remaining terminal jobs.

↑ Back to contents

sections.title: Cloud providers
sections.text:
Open Settings → Model Providers. Add the endpoint, wire protocol, actual model ID and API credential supplied by your provider. Test the configuration, enable both provider and model, choose the default Agent model, then verify the model label on New Task.

Provider and model names may contain hyphens, underscores and version dots, such as qwen3.5-plus or model_v2.1. Keep the actual model ID exactly as supplied. Provider display names normalize pasted line breaks and incidental invisible formatting while preserving meaningful Unicode; oversized names report their UTF-8 size.

If a model is missing, check provider/model switches and “Hide from main model list.” Hiding preserves auxiliary uses; disabling prevents new selections. Provider calls may incur third-party charges. Credentials belong in Keychain, never project files, screenshots or public issues.

Floe validates the form before it writes anything. An invalid field is reported in your language, no write starts and the form keeps its content. A local save and an iCloud upload are reported separately: “Saved on this device; iCloud sync is pending” means the configuration is committed locally and the upload can be retried — it is not a failed save, and you do not need to re-enter an API key. Remote records that fail validation are skipped while the local copy is kept.

In Add text/image/video, tap the Provider field itself to open ONE searchable selector: the built-in provider presets (including an explicit manual/custom choice) and the verified catalog entries live in the same list and are filtered together as you type (aliases and configured badges included). There is no separate preset row, no "add from catalog" button and no separate catalog page. Choosing an entry closes the selector and preserves everything else you already entered, including a custom display name. Selecting a vendor that genuinely supports more than one service role raises a one-time Additional uses prompt where the role you started with is fixed and every extra role is opt-in; choose Configure, Not now, or dismiss the sheet — a declined role is not offered again. Extra roles share this connection's endpoint and API key only when the origin, protocol family and auth style really match; a different origin is shown as Configure separately with its own visible settings. Changing the connection identity (scheme/host/port/provider family/auth style) clears the typed key and refuses to silently reuse a stored key across connections.

Catalog metadata is verified per model, not promised for a whole provider. A model you add now starts with the capabilities the bundled catalog actually verified for it (for example image input for a vision-capable model). Models you saved before that metadata existed are never rewritten silently: Floe offers a one-time Model capability updates review that lists each model and the exact capability it would gain (Before → After) and writes nothing until you choose Apply updates (or Not now). A capability you set yourself is recorded as your own decision — a later catalog refresh or iCloud sync never flips it back, and a capability you switched off stays off. "Supports text/images/video" describes the roles the catalog verifies for that entry, not a tested live inference: the first real request is still the compatibility check. GitHub Copilot, Azure, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex are not offered when adding a new provider — Floe cannot execute them without OAuth or deployment-scoped endpoints — but connections you already saved to those providers stay listed and editable.

Models that support it also carry a reasoning/thinking effort setting. With Automatic, Floe asks your configured auxiliary text model once when a fresh round starts to choose an effort for that request; the decision is kept for the round, including guide/steer and continuation messages, and is not reclassified mid-round. A manual effort you choose is never changed. If no auxiliary model is configured, or the helper fails or times out, Floe falls back to the model's own supported default.

Volcengine pay-as-you-go and Agent Plan, and Alibaba Cloud pay-as-you-go and Token Plan, are separate provider choices. Select the plan you purchased; each keeps its own endpoint, key and models. Saving or testing one does not switch to another billing channel.

Choose subscription models from the public catalog or enter a model ID manually; candidates do not establish your account's entitlement. Test connection sends one small request to your selected chat model and may count toward plan usage. Opening or saving settings does not generate images or videos. Volcengine Agent Plan image candidates are separate from pay-as-you-go models; its video entry is not offered in this update. Alibaba pay-as-you-go and Token Plan use their respective image and video services. A submitted video keeps its existing task ID; a failed status lookup does not submit another paid generation.

sections.title: Web search providers
sections.text:
DeepSeek Search is available as a separate provider with its own key and an option to include page content. Long summaries and content are retained as returned by the service. The interface shows a concise projection; the assistant can use the full result within its context capacity or read further. Search summaries still need source verification.

Settings → Web Search lists only providers you have added. Use Add Provider to choose a service or a compatible custom interface, configure an account and test a search. Each saved account has its own switch and priority. Refresh the provider directory from the add screen or Settings → Updates; downloaded directory updates preserve saved accounts and keys. Preset provider names follow directory updates automatically; names you edit yourself are preserved. Review other available changes before applying them to an existing account.

Search returns five results when no count is specified and keeps the interface summary concise. Enabled professional datasets use the same search tool and selected account when the current task permits them. Ordinary text and voice chat discover and call enabled, authorized tools; professional datasets still require their configured account and permissions. Temporary chat keeps its read boundary. Leaving continuous voice preserves the original conversation mode.

In the Volcengine editor, choose the account that matches your key:

• Agent Plan Doubao Search — an Agent Plan key, with optional Professional datasets (off by default and independent of the main search switch; the editor shows its real connection state).
• Ark Responses — an ordinary Ark API key. Under Search engine, Doubao Search Custom uses the Doubao search engine, while Online content uses Toutiao, Douyin encyclopedia and Moji weather together.
• Doubao Search API — a separate Doubao Search key.
• Custom endpoint (legacy) — an existing custom endpoint.

Online content enables all three sources together, without individual switches. Query rewrite and Authoritative sources only are available for Agent Plan and Doubao Search API. Your existing default search provider and priority are unchanged.

sections.title: Vision, generation and image editing
sections.text:
Settings → Auxiliary Models configures image understanding, image generation and image editing separately. Text support does not imply any of these capabilities. Attach the source image before requesting an edit.

For small text, dimension labels or other fine details, ask the assistant to view a region of the original image. The local view preserves the source file and provides the chosen region to the current visual workflow. Ask for a fresh screenshot after changing a model or page; an earlier capture represents its earlier state.

sections.title: Apple and downloaded models
sections.text:
Apple's system model is managed by the OS. Follow the availability reason shown by Floe: device support, Apple Intelligence settings or model readiness. Floe has no download button for that system model.

Downloaded MLX models are Beta. Download, load and inference are separate stages; start with short text before multi-turn work. The local path uses text and bounded OCR of attachments, not semantic image understanding. Linux guests and local models share device memory. Review any request to release resources; cancelling does not authorize stopping another task. Disabling keeps files; deleting removes downloads. Preserve current diagnostics after a crash instead of clearing all data.

↑ Back to contents

sections.title: 3. Tasks and workspace ownership
sections.text:
On New Task, check the model, project, execution target, Skills and permissions before sending. With no project, Floe creates a private task workspace; with a project, file actions belong to that project. Attach necessary material and state the outcome, format, location and completion criteria.

Example: “Read this attachment, create a one-page summary and action list in the current workspace, and give me links to the finished files.” The draft becomes a continuing task. Later messages use the same task context.

Authorize external folders through the system file picker; writing a path in chat does not grant access. Deleting a private task may remove its private workspace. Deleting a project task differs from deleting project files. Export important results first. Notes stores its own documents independently of chat deletion.

↑ Back to contents

sections.title: 4. Conversation, Plan, Goal and recovery
sections.text:
Mode | Purpose | What to do
Agent | Execute work | State the outcome; inspect permissions, tools and files
Plan | Discuss a proposed approach | Review and accept it before treating any step as executed
Goal | Work across stages | Define steps, budget and completion evidence

Return inserts a new line; Command+Return sends where supported. Text wraps at the available width and Expand appears on the third line. Further input keeps your typing position visible. The full editor shares the same draft. Messages during a run can correct requirements without creating another task.

Answering questions. The assistant can show a question card in the current task. Answer one question at a time by selecting, typing or dictating. Required questions wait for your reply. Optional questions can remain open during independent work, or wait for a specified interval before the assistant uses an explicitly identified assumption. Silence never means consent and an answer does not grant action permissions. With notifications allowed, supported questions accept a background inline reply. Temporary-chat questions stay in the current session only.

Hardware keyboard. In Settings → General, choose whether Return adds a new line or sends a message. When Return sends, Shift–Return adds a new line. Command–Return still sends. The choice applies to the inline and expanded message composers; the onscreen keyboard keeps its existing behavior.

Selecting and finding text. Long-press your message or an assistant reply to select text, adjust the selection and copy. Choose Find in Chat from the conversation menu, or press Command+F. Previous and Next jump between highlighted hits without changing your draft. The sidebar search also finds saved ordinary conversations. Multiple words must all match; quoted phrases stay together. Results show the actual matching line.

Scheduled tasks. A linked plan appears below the conversation navigation bar. Open it for timing, parameters and run history. Each occurrence creates its own task. Run Now adds an extra run without changing the original time. Skip Next skips that occurrence; Cancel Future keeps existing history. A successful occurrence does not itself complete the overall goal: the assistant must explicitly finish a plan whose goal is achieved. Live Activities may show running work or the nearest wait; delivery and execution timing remain subject to system scheduling.

After background interruption, return to the original task, inspect the last tool receipt and use Resume or send “Continue.” Verify uncertain uploads, submissions or other side effects before repeating them. Returning to the foreground does not mean an old process survived. A bounded pause or an unknown side-effect outcome needs deliberate recovery: inspect or reconcile the last receipt, then resume. A read-only check alone does not automatically re-arm paused work.

Scroll up to read history without following new output; return to the bottom to resume following. Long-press a sidebar conversation to open its actions, then choose Multi-select to show selection circles; Done leaves selection mode. Pin and Unpin are in the same menu. Pinned conversations stay at the top of their own group, including after restarting.

Batch management is also available in Task Center and Settings → Data management → Manage tasks. Selection and Select All apply only to the tasks visible under the current filter and search. Archiving asks for confirmation, states that it stops the selected tasks' own running work first, and archived tasks can be restored later from the same screen (switch to Archived) or the archive list; deleting also stops their own work and removes each task's private workspace while shared project files stay. Each task reports its own result — failed or unverified tasks stay selected for retry — and a running batch can be stopped without touching unprocessed tasks.

↑ Back to contents

sections.title: 5. Permissions and verification
sections.text:
Tool cards show the progress and results of actions. Review the target and effects when a permission request appears. Earlier tool activity loads as you scroll, without a separate history expansion button. Individual tool cards still expand to show their details.

• Expand a tool card and inspect its target, workspace and result.
• Review the object and side effect before allowing a permission request.
• Open generated files. For editable documents, save, close and reopen.
• Check remote command exit codes and host identity. “Started” is not “completed.”
• Report what actually happened with redacted evidence when an outcome differs.

Ordinary Office, PDF, image, video and CAD edits within the task’s authorized local scope can proceed without a confirmation for every step. Revision checks, recoverable saves and output verification still apply. Writes into a code repository, unresolved targets, explicit destructive overwrites, external sends and protected PDF actions retain their applicable review or consent. A request to preview or review a proposal still waits for adoption.

Native 3D document editing, including geometry, materials, assemblies and animations, requires no additional human or model review, including for a CAD document stored in a repository. File access, revision checks and undo still apply; exported files keep their normal destination checks.

Routine commands in the task’s resolved local Linux guest receive fewer repeated reviews; this does not treat the Mac host as a disposable guest. Risky remote-machine changes remain subject to the existing review policy. Shared guest sessions keep separate ownership and cancellation, and stopping or resetting an environment is a separate operation.

Documents, websites, tool results and memory cannot grant new permissions. Never follow embedded instructions to expose credentials or broaden access.

Delegated subagents run with the same effective permissions as the current task: the explore/research/execute choice is a focus hint, not a permission level, and every child call goes through the same approval, workspace, environment and mutation-serialization path as the main task. A subagent can never delegate again or create a new user-visible task — delegate and conversation.spawn are main-task-only and are refused at execution time, not merely hidden. Sibling subagents of one task may exchange bounded messages; a message is untrusted data, never a permission grant, and cannot restart a subagent that has finished.

A subagent can independently use tools.list / tools.search and skill.list / skill.search / skill.read. It loads the tools and workflow instructions needed for its task instead of receiving the entire tool catalog in every request. Skills can guide scripts, native tools and configured MCP use within the same task permissions; reading a Skill does not grant new permissions. Known tools do not require a guide to be read first.

Several task clients — the parent run and its children — may share one Linux environment through separate processes and execution sessions. Results, working directories, standard input/output and cancellation belong to the requesting session: cancelling one child does not stop the other consumers, and stopping the whole environment is a separate lifecycle action. Writes to the same known target follow the same coordination as ordinary task edits.
